findings.title: enableSqlExpressions silently ignores the feature flag with misleading dead logic
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (the variable actually means "disabled") and then returns `false` on both branches. The feature-flag lookup is therefore dead code, and the function name/branching suggests the flag still controls the feature when it does not. Operators who enable `sqlExpressions` get the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented" with no indication the flag is intentionally inert. If the intent is to hard-disable the feature, the function should simply return false (or be removed and the case made unconditional) with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264, and the flag registration/docs should say it is currently non-functional; otherwise a future reader may 'fix' the obvious-looking bug and re-enable the path.

findings.title: Legacy rawNode path reports a misleading 'error reading SQL command' instead of 'not implemented'
findings.body: `UnmarshalSQLCommand` (the non-reader path used by the existing SSE node parser) still calls `NewSQLCommand`, which now calls `sql.TablesList` -> stub `RunCommands` returning `errors.New("not implemented")`. That error is logged at Warn as "invalid sql query" and surfaced to users as `sql-invalid-sql` / "error reading SQL command". Users with existing SQL expression nodes will be told their SQL is invalid rather than that the feature is disabled, and server logs will fill with spurious 'invalid sql query' warnings. The two code paths should return the same explicit 'SQL expressions are disabled/not implemented' error.

findings.title: No test asserting SQL expressions are rejected on both parse paths
findings.body: This is a security fix (CVE-2024-9264) that is supposed to guarantee SQL expressions can never execute, yet no test is added verifying that `ReadQuery` with `QueryTypeSQL` returns an error even when `FlagSqlExpressions` is enabled, nor that `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand` fails, nor that `sql.DB.QueryFramesInto` returns an error. Without regression tests, a later refactor (e.g., someone 'fixing' the odd `enableSqlExpressions` logic or re-adding a real DB implementation behind the flag) could silently re-open the RCE/LFI path.

findings.title: Parser retains unreachable DuckDB-specific code after stubbing the DB
findings.body: `TablesList` still builds a DuckDB-specific `SELECT json_serialize_sql(...)` command and `tablesFromAST`/`astError`/`existsInList` remain, but `RunCommands` is now a stub that always errors, so everything after line 27 is unreachable. Keeping DuckDB-shaped code alive while the dependency has been removed for security reasons invites someone to re-wire a DuckDB backend into `NewInMemoryDB` without revisiting the vulnerability. Either remove the dead code or clearly document that the stub is intentional.
